messages:
Aisha Patel: @channel hey! first day — trying to enroll my Surface Pro 9 (serial S12345) into Intune via Company Portal. OOBE completed but Company Portal shows 'Enrollment failed (0x80180014)'. BitLocker also says 'suspended' and I'm not admin. Any tips? :wave:

Jamal (IT): Welcome Aisha! @Aisha Patel — sorry for the hassle. 0x80180014 usually means the device couldn't register to Azure AD during MDM enrollment. Can you open an elevated PowerShell and run:

```
dsregcmd /status
``` 

and paste the AAD join status output? Also confirm Company Portal app version.

Aisha Patel: Pasted output below — not sure which bits matter:

```
DeviceId : 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
Name : WIN-SURFACE
WorkplaceJoined : NO
AzureAdJoined : NO
TenantId : 
```

Lina (IT-Support): that shows it didn't join AAD. Two quick checks: 1) Is the device on your home VPN? If yes, disconnect and try again; conditional access can block enrollments. 2) Did you sign in with your corporate email in the Company Portal (not a personal account)?

Aisha Patel: I was on my home VPN. Disconnected and retried — Company Portal now asks to 'Set up device' and prompts for a PIN, but then errors with a different popup: 'BitLocker cannot be enabled, TPM not found'. :thinking_face:

Alex (Security): For Surfaces, TPM should be on by default. If the firmware disabled it, we can ask you to toggle a setting in UEFI. But before we ask that, can you run:

```
manage-bde -status C:\n```

and paste the first few lines (State and TPM status)?

Aisha Patel: Output:

```
Volume C: [OS]
[OS Volume]
Size: 237 GB
BitLocker Version: None
Percentage Encrypted: 0%
TPM detected: No
```

Jamal (IT): OK TPM detected: No — sounds like firmware turned off the TPM or it's disabled for virtualization. Two options: 1) We can give you a one-time local admin to finish enrollment and re-enable TPM from Windows Security > Device Security > Security processor > Security processor details > Clear TPM (we'll guide). 2) Or we can do a remote UEFI session. Which do you prefer? :call_me_hand:

Maya (Manager): Aisha — do option 1 if you're comfortable. Jamal, pls only grant temp admin for 30 minutes and log the action.

Aisha Patel: I can do option 1. Thanks! How do I get temp admin?

Lina (IT-Support): I'll create a time-limited admin token. Give me your device serial (on the sticker or Settings > System > About). Also tell us a 10-minute window when you can be available.

Aisha Patel: Serial S12345 (same as above). I'm free in 15 minutes for 30 minutes.

it-setup-bot: Admin token created. Token ID: ADM-TKN-98765. Expires in 30 minutes.

Jamal (IT): Ok Aisha, open an elevated PowerShell and run (copy/paste):

```
New-LocalUser -Name "temp_admin_aisha" -NoPassword
Add-LocalGroupMember -Group "Administrators" -Member "temp_admin_aisha"
```

Then sign out and sign back in as your regular user and accept the UAC prompt when Company Portal asks. We'll monitor.

Aisha Patel: done. I could re-run Company Portal — it completed AAD join! Now BitLocker went through and TPM shows present. manage-bde output now:

```
TPM detected: Yes
Percentage Encrypted: 100%
Volume Status: Fully Encrypted
```

Alex (Security): Nice. Jamal, please remove the temp admin account and record the removal.

Jamal (IT): Removing now.

```
Remove-LocalUser -Name "temp_admin_aisha"
```

Jamal (IT): Removal logged. Enrollment completed, device AAD-joined and Intune profile applied. :tada:

Maya (Manager): Awesome — welcome aboard Aisha! Ping me if you still need app installs.

Aisha Patel: Thank you everyone! Saved me a trip to IT. :heart:

it-setup-bot: Enrollment event recorded: device S12345 joined tenant redwood.onmicrosoft.com at 1718215530
